motivation: New encoders frequently win the first 808-row comparison and lose on subsequent panels. Test whether distributing opportunities between broad nomination and repeated checks can improve the quality of the final decision itself.
bank: Freeze every complete, row-aligned, fitting-only probability file from the prefix-listed tree, TabICL, neural, boosting, rank, Bayesian, rule, measurement, Mitra, semantic, binding and distillation screens. The retained research reference is the equal original aligned-tree and TabICL pair. Each challenger may receive share .125, .25, .5 or 1. Identical probability banks count once. No new model fits.
episodes: Independently of predictions, split the 2432 feedback-panel rows into six exact-feature-group stratified folds with seed 583257. In each rotation hold one fold out for scoring, use the next two for first nomination and the remaining three for successive confirmation. Every row is scored once. Each feedback episode has at most 48 model-panel reads: one per distinct candidate initially and three per shortlisted candidate, at most four. Cached incumbent evidence is common to all policies. No new training or model API.
actions: First nominate the best share per candidate by corrected minus lost labels on the two nomination portions together, tie toward the smaller share, then towards reduced Brier loss and a deterministic key. Retain the four best distinct challengers even if they have yet to show a lift. Lock these shares. Compare a nomination-only action, a pooled-best action that aggregates all available evidence, and a protected action on the identical evidence. Protected adoption needs positive changes in two of the three confirmation panels, no panel loss greater than .005, mean confirmation gain at least .003, and a positive lower one-standard-error bound for grouped paired differences. Otherwise retain the existing reference. The outer fold is not consulted for its own decision.
scope: A retrospective decision replay on the same previous development rows. Counts describe these frozen predictions; the different outer decisions share training evidence. They are not new data or six independent tasks. All choices are written before any of the six outer scores are computed. A promising rule still needs a prospective cold ordinary-entry study.
